direction.premise: A shared picture puzzle turns each drag path into a temporary obstacle for the other mosaic builders.
direction.composition: A square picture grid stays above a compact tray of the viewer’s assigned fragments; room, time and completion sit in a single top row.
direction.shapeLanguage: Rounded picture tiles, a literal square cell grid and translucent colored trail cells expose ownership and blocked paths.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Recovered authored SVG puzzle illustrations are sliced into picture fragments; trails remain translucent overlays rather than decorative glow.
direction.paletteLogic: Each builder has a colored outline and path; the source picture colors remain intact so matching fragments is a spatial task.
direction.typography: Quiet source labels identify the tray and progress, with numerical room and timer chips kept separate from the illustration.
direction.signature: Dragging a fragment paints a visible path that blocks other players for thirty seconds, even after the piece lands.
direction.distinction: FOG uses geographic orders and ZAMAZKA uses painted restoration fragments; this port retains its source game object and the specific input loop described here.

architecture.primaryVerb: Drag only your assigned picture fragments to their correct cells while choosing routes around other players’ fading trails.
architecture.physicalFeedback: The held fragment follows the pointer, visited cells gain a colored trail and a correct drop raises shared completion.
architecture.spatialRationale: A square picture grid stays above a compact tray of the viewer’s assigned fragments; room, time and completion sit in a single top row. This keeps the current game object and its real inputs spatially connected on a phone.

production.renderer: DOM picture tiles cut from the recovered SVG art preserve crisp illustrations and direct pointer dragging on phones.
production.focalAsset: The original SVG puzzle catalog is preserved and cut at runtime into square fragments; the authored mosaic SVG supplies install identity.

motion.character: The held fragment follows the pointer, visited cells gain a colored trail and a correct drop raises shared completion.
motion.action: Drag only your assigned picture fragments to their correct cells while choosing routes around other players’ fading trails.
motion.anticipation: The current selection, room state and available control labels expose the pending operation before the player activates it.
motion.response: The next visible state responds to the actual control: Dragging a fragment paints a visible path that blocks other players for thirty seconds, even after the piece lands.
motion.followThrough: The resulting world, board or round state remains visible until a later explicit action changes it; no decorative transition hides the outcome.
motion.interruption: Repeated input uses the current state; pointer cancellation releases held controls and hidden tabs stop transmitting held actions.
motion.reducedMotion: The complete play state remains legible without decorative entry animations; spatial gameplay and authoritative outcomes retain their original timing.

evidence.expectedChange: An offline solo puzzle lobby opens; starting it assigns every fragment to the local builder.
